name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: A motor-driven vehicle capable of cross-country travel over natural terrain without a road, such as a dirt bike or ATV; any vehicle the BMV registers for the road is excluded. An electric dirt bike or e-moto that isn't registered as a motorcycle or motor driven cycle is an off-road vehicle.

restrictions.rule: Capable of cross-country travel without a road, powered by anything other than muscle or wind; no limit on motor power or speed (Indiana Code §14-8-2-185)
Not an electric bicycle, which is exempt from off-road vehicle rules (Indiana Code §14-8-2-185)

Registered with the BMV for $30 every three years, with two decals on its forward half and the registration certificate carried while riding; it must have a manufacturer's identification number (IC 9-18.1-14)
Titled with the BMV if bought after December 31, 2009

Not allowed on public roads or parking lots, except to cross a non-limited-access highway at a right angle after stopping, on a road's right-of-way away from the traveled lanes, or on county roads a county or local ordinance opens to them (IC 14-16-1-20)
A driver's license is needed wherever it's ridden on a public highway (IC 14-16-1-20)
Riders under 14 need the immediate supervision of someone 18 or older, except on land they or their parent own or control (IC 14-16-1-20)
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet (IC 9-18.1-14-11)
A headlight and taillight from sunset to sunrise, and adequate brakes (IC 14-16-1-21)
Ridden on public land only with the managing agency's consent, and on private land only with the owner's (IC 14-16-1-23, 14-16-1-27)

DNR's riding areas are Redbird and Interlake State Recreation Areas, which need a trail pass per vehicle; at Redbird every rider wears a DOT helmet and dirt bike riders under 16 must be directly supervised by a parent or guardian, and out-of-state riders may buy a $20 annual permit instead of registering
